method: Read frozen task.md, reference.md and rubric.json for each case.
Read every mathematical source module and the declared coverage, including actual definitions, constructor bodies and boundary witnesses.
Check the main declarations against original assumptions and quantifiers; follow abstract helper applications into the actual objects.
Check that construction or obstruction conclusions are derived rather than stored as input certificate fields.
Inspect the four dynamic audit modules; leave kernel execution results to the independent build evidence.

MG-R001.main_target: The proposed total pointwise unique fixed family with a finite uniform geometric bound is false under the original hypotheses.

checks.obligation: Original extended pseudometrics and the isolated absorbing point
checks.assessment: Gauge contains only the supplied distance axioms. Option adds a bottom point with infinite distance to every nonbottom point; absorbingEquiv identifies that encoding with any original pointed carrier. Separation, completeness and finite distances are not assumed.

checks.obligation: Actual partition, input transfer and unfolding
checks.assessment: The partition fields are precisely local data. Selection of a call edge is justified by the cover and same-source disjointness, and actual transfer outputs lie in the target input subset. No solution, termination or convergence field is stored.

checks.obligation: Actual block matrix and extended function-space bounds
checks.assessment: delta is the supremum over the actual input type, coeff is the sum over edges with the stated source and target, and the matrix estimate is proved for actual iterates. Path products have the outer-to-inner return order. All bounds stay in ENNReal with zero-times-infinity equal to zero.

checks.obligation: Weights and contraction derived from the spectral hypothesis
checks.assessment: The positive weights are constructed from a finite power sum of the actual nonnegative matrix after Gelfand decay. The contraction inequality on all function families is derived from the local estimate, not supplied as an additional certificate.

checks.obligation: Finite-residual and finite-distance conclusions remain conditional
checks.assessment: Cauchy convergence requires an explicit finite weighted residual and q<1. Fixed-point comparison requires finite distance and concludes zero component distances, not pointwise equality. No original-space limit is asserted without completeness.

checks.obligation: Least partial solution and precise finite-termination domain
checks.assessment: The construction takes values in Option Y and uses actual finite evaluations. Its leastness is in the bottom information order, and its nonbottom domain is proved equivalent to the inductively defined finite call termination. It is not represented as a total nonabsorbing solution.

checks.obligation: Full two-dimensional counterexample satisfies original premises
checks.assessment: The output is real two-space with two coordinate gauges; the input integers are explicitly transported to the subset {(n,0)}. The two-edge matrix is proved equal to the actual block aggregate after reindexing, with spectral radius exactly one half. Option provides the required absorbing extension.

checks.obligation: Literal nonuniqueness and failure at every finite unfolding depth
checks.assessment: Distinct real parameters give distinct actual fixed families. The specified legal initial family has infinite supremum error at each depth, including depth one, so no finite error constant works. StrongClosure includes the requested quantifiers, literal uniqueness and a single geometric ratio for all initial families.

checks.obligation: Pointwise convergence, dependence restoration and smaller existence obstructions
checks.assessment: The additional claims use actual iterates and the stated small spaces. The two no-fixed-point examples retain the spectral hypothesis after singleton-input transport. The zero-distance example does not confuse equality with equality in the separation quotient.

checks.obligation: Pointwise termination does not force uniform finite depth
checks.assessment: The finite one-loop system on natural-number inputs terminates for every input, yet no common evaluation depth succeeds. Its actual aggregate has spectral radius zero.

accepted_encodings: Nonabsorbing output carrier Y with Option Y for the isolated bottom.
Typed input domains and explicit equivalences to the original subsets.
Finite-index iSup is the requested maximum; NNReal constants are precisely finite nonnegative real constants.
scope_notes: The conjunction of the original target is refuted. The positive conditional statements and the partial solution are kept separate from that false target.

MG-R004.main_target: Vanishing reduced records in a finite-length complex of complex Hilbert spaces does not imply bounded chain contraction or bounded Laplacian right inverses.
MG-R004.main_target_verdict: faithfully refuted; full finite closed-range criterion verified

checks.obligation: Actual complex Hilbert counterexample with both endpoint records zero
checks.assessment: H is complex lp with exponent two, and d is the actual complex-linear diagonal with weights 1/(n+1). The kernel is zero and the norm closure of its range is the full space. These are exactly the two endpoint reduced-record conditions for r=1; no finite-dimensional assumption is used.

checks.obligation: Actual bounded contraction and Laplacian obstruction
checks.assessment: Unit-vector bounds rule out a bounded left inverse. Injectivity relates a right inverse to a left inverse. The actual adjoint and both degree Laplacians are computed, and their bounded right inverses are ruled out on these same spaces.

checks.obligation: Reduced acyclicity gives only Laplacian injectivity
checks.assessment: The zero kernel follows from the energy identity and orthogonality to the closure of the incoming range. A right inverse is then proved to be a two-sided inverse; no lower bound or surjectivity is inferred from injectivity alone.

checks.obligation: Closed ranges construct actual partial inverses and chain contraction
checks.assessment: The restriction from ker(A)-orthogonal-complement to range(A) is proved bijective by orthogonal decomposition. Closed range supplies completeness and the bounded inverse theorem. The returned partial inverse is composed with the actual orthogonal projection; the two projection formulas yield the contraction.

checks.obligation: Actual coercive bound and bounded Laplacian inverse
checks.assessment: M is max(1, norms of the two constructed partial inverses), and the proved lower bound is M^(-2). Closed range plus orthogonal-complement triviality proves surjectivity before constructing the continuous linear equivalence. The inverse norm bound is at most M squared.

checks.obligation: Finite complex indexing and endpoints
checks.assessment: Original H_j is represented by H(j+1); H(0) and H(r+2) are zero spaces. The finite theorem uses only degree equations 0..r and ranges 0..r+1, and imposes no tail exactness or tail closed-range condition. Both s endpoint maps are explicitly zero. The result also permits zero intermediate spaces.

checks.obligation: All directions of the finite three-way criterion
checks.assessment: Contraction forces the incoming image to equal the kernel. Closed ranges produce contraction and both-sided Laplacian inverses. Degreewise right inverses yield left inverses using reduced exactness, then closedness of each outgoing range; the incoming zero map and terminal zero map are handled separately. Thus the criterion covers precisely the finite complex.

checks.obligation: Adjoint-times-inverse formula and stability
checks.assessment: The formula uses actual consecutive differentials and their zero composites. The local degree lemma includes zero endpoint maps. Common constants are finite sums of the actual finitely many operator norms, a valid bound in place of the reference maxima.

checks.obligation: Finite-dimensional subclass remains conditional
checks.assessment: Finite-dimensionality appears only in the explicitly additional sufficient branch, where it proves closed ranges; it is absent from the original counterexample and general finite criterion.

accepted_encodings: Zero reduced quotient is expressed by equality of the closed boundary space with the kernel.
A natural-number family pads the finite complex by zero endpoint spaces; finite_criteria does not assume an infinite exact complex.
scope_notes: Non-surjectivity of the diagonal is proved via the bounded inverse theorem and explicit unit-vector obstruction. The reference vector (1/n) is not separately encoded; the same non-surjectivity conclusion is fully proved by this alternative route.
The finite target constructs a partial-inverse contraction; the reference adjoint-times-inverse contraction is proved by the separate universally quantified degree lemma.

MG-R006.main_target: Finite quotient records and surjective B and C transitions do not ensure surjectivity at the inverse-limit level.
MG-R006.main_target_verdict: faithfully refuted; natural obstruction theory verified

checks.obligation: Original abelian groups, actual products and inverse limits
checks.assessment: delta is x_n-alpha_n(x_(n+1)), the inverse limit is its actual kernel, and all induced maps apply the given row maps coordinatewise. Injectivity and middle exactness are proved from row exactness and the supplied commuting diagrams.

checks.obligation: Choice-independent actual obstruction quotient
checks.assessment: The target group is the quotient of the actual product by the image of delta. Local defects are extracted using row exactness, two choices differ by an actual coboundary, and additivity is proved using sums of lifts.

checks.obligation: Vanishing iff actual compatible lift and nonempty-fiber freedom
checks.assessment: The reverse implication corrects the chosen lifts by an actual product of kernel elements. The freedom theorem quantifies two existing compatible lifts and yields a unique compatible kernel difference; it never obtains existence from uniqueness or chooses a canonical origin.

checks.obligation: Terminal surjectivity and exact obstruction criterion
checks.assessment: Surjectivity of B transitions is used in an explicit recursive choice of preimages to prove delta_B surjective. Consequently the obstruction homomorphism is surjective. Kernel-transition surjectivity is an explicitly additional sufficient hypothesis, not deduced from B or C.

checks.obligation: Naturality under all exact-tower morphisms
checks.assessment: The actual product map descends to the quotient because it takes coboundaries to coboundaries. The connecting map commutes with arbitrary compatible maps of A, B and C towers by transporting local lifts and their defects.

checks.obligation: Counterexample preserves every original premise
checks.assessment: C_n is the finite group ZMod(2^(n+1)), A_n is the actual subgroup 2^(n+1)Z, B_n is Z, beta is identity, and gamma is natural reduction. Row exactness, finiteness, both stated transition surjectivities and both commuting squares are realized, not only postulated.

checks.obligation: Explicit incompatible record and all finite prefixes
checks.assessment: The record is the multiplicative inverse of three modulo each power of two. Compatibility follows from uniqueness. Every finite prefix has a single integer representative, whereas a global compatible lift would give one integer b with all powers of two dividing 3b-1, forcing the impossible equation 3b=1.

checks.obligation: Kernel freedom zero does not repair existence
checks.assessment: The kernel limit is proved zero, the B limit is explicitly additively equivalent to Z, and nontriviality of the actual obstruction quotient is instantiated from the established non-surjectivity and general criterion.

accepted_encodings: Lean index zero represents the first row, so exponent n+1 matches the reference exponent n.
Short exactness is encoded by injectivity, surjectivity and range-equals-kernel on the actual row maps.
scope_notes: The obstruction theory holds for general abelian towers. Finiteness of C is supplied in the counterexample, where it is needed to preserve the original premises.

MG-R007.main_target: Coherent equivariant sections exist and yield the required equivariant limit decomposition; all choices and their whole-tower transport are classified.

checks.obligation: Original arbitrary-characteristic representation setting
checks.assessment: The theorem uses actual Representation and IntertwiningMap. It assumes the original local equivariant sections, finite-dimensional C and B_n, the row exactness and commuting diagrams. It allows any monoid G and does not require finite-dimensional A_n, both genuine weakenings of the supplied hypotheses. There is no averaging or transition-surjectivity assumption.

checks.obligation: Stabilization is derived and instantiated on the actual section problem
checks.assessment: Actual composites form a decreasing chain of submodule images. Finite-dimensionality supplies Artinian stabilization, after which the stable fibers have surjective transitions proved using late-stage preimages. Recursive choice produces a point. coherent_sections applies this theorem to the actual finite-dimensional spaces Hom_G(C,B_n) and postcomposition maps with target id_C.

checks.obligation: Original limit objects and quotient record
checks.assessment: The objects are the submodules of compatible coordinate families, with coordinatewise action. i_infinity applies the original i_n, and q_infinity is the first original q_n. The latter equals each coordinate record by compatibility.

checks.obligation: Actual compatible direct-sum isomorphism
checks.assessment: The kernel preimages are constructed coordinatewise and injectivity of i_n forces their compatibility. The section is assembled from the coherent sections. The product-to-limit map is i_infinity(a)+s_infinity(c), its bijectivity is derived, and the original inclusion and projection equations are both explicit conclusions.

checks.obligation: All sections and unique kernel freedom
checks.assessment: Every difference factors uniquely through the actual equivariant kernel map. At the limit this gives exactly Hom_G(C,A_infinity). Coordinate extraction and assembly are inverse, including the definitional coordinate-of-assembly direction, so the classification includes all coherent families as well as every limit section. The same generic coordinate construction applies to the A tower and gives the stated compatible-Hom identification.

checks.obligation: All decompositions with the prescribed inclusion and projection
checks.assessment: Any such equivalence has section c -> e(0,c) and equals splitMap of that section. Uniqueness of this section follows by evaluating the displayed equality at (0,c); no extra decomposition choices remain unclassified.

checks.obligation: Whole-tower transport of the full solution space and freedom
checks.assessment: Conjugation b_n s_n d^(-1) preserves both equation families. Inverse diagram isomorphisms give the actual inverse bijection. The formula for kernel translations uses a_n u_n d^(-1), and identity/composition are proved. The generic coherent-map transport applies to the A tower too. Natural transport of the space is not represented as a natural preferred point.

checks.obligation: Non-surjective transitions still satisfy the given split rows
checks.assessment: The actual product row is short exact and the collapse transition preserves the quotient and sends every section parameter to zero. It is proved not surjective.

checks.obligation: Modular and infinite-dimensional boundaries
checks.assessment: The characteristic-p example is a genuine representation of the cyclic group of prime order with an actual nonsplit short exact row. It is only used after deleting the local-splitting premise. The polynomial example has actual split rows and diagram maps but no compatible section, proved by coefficients; it only tests deletion of finite-dimensionality.

checks.obligation: No natural preferred section and degenerate spaces
checks.assessment: The actual shear automorphism has no fixed section and preserves inclusion and projection. The general construction permits zero spaces, while the two boundary lemmas give uniqueness for zero quotient or zero kernel. Existence remains supplied by the main theorem.

accepted_encodings: Two-summand algebraic direct sum is represented by the usual product module, equivalent for two summands.
The finite-dimensional affine argument is implemented as the fiber of a linear map in the actual equivariant-Hom space.
Infinite compatible section and translation spaces are handled through coordinate assembly, not an unjustified exchange-of-limits theorem.
scope_notes: Local equivariant splitting is exactly an original premise, while global coherence is a proved conclusion.
No natural preferred section, surjective module transitions, surjective original section-space transitions, or characteristic restriction is added.
